convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom with unknown indicator 'AFL_WinnerSign' which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. Also includes two external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) providing custom trade management and smoothing algorithms. The AFL_WinnerSign indicator logic is opaque and must be manually reimplemented in Python.

derived_values.name: UpValue - AFL_WinnerSign buffer 1 buy signal
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(handle, 1, SignalBar, 1, UpValue) — non-zero and != EMPTY_VALUE means buy signal

derived_values.name: DnValue - AFL_WinnerSign buffer 0 sell signal
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(handle, 0, SignalBar, 1, DnValue) — non-zero and != EMPTY_VALUE means sell signal

other_exits: Opposing signal closes position: UpValue signal closes short, DnValue signal closes long. Additional lookback scan from SignalBar+1 to Bars checks for opposing signals if both open and close flags are enabled and no close signal found on current bar.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum selects sizing method; LOT mode uses fixed lot fraction of 0.1

custom_logic_notes: The AFL_WinnerSign custom indicator must be fully reimplemented. It uses configurable smoothing (SMA/EMA/SMMA/LWMA/JJMA/JurX/ParMA/T3/VIDYA/AMA via SmoothAlgorithms.mqh), applied price types (9 custom price types beyond standard 7), and volume type selection. The EA has a lookback scan mechanism: if both open and close flags are enabled for a side and no close signal is found on the SignalBar, it scans forward bars (SignalBar+1 to Bars) for an opposing signal to trigger close. Signal bar is configurable (default=1 meaning previous bar). BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose boolean inputs gate which actions are allowed. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar utilities.
backtest_data_needs: Any symbol H6 730 days with tick volume
python_conversion_notes: Must reverse-engineer or find AFL_WinnerSign indicator source to reimplement in Python. The indicator uses the SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library which implements 10 smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA beyond standard MAs). The AFL_WinnerSign indicator logic likely combines a weighted/average price with smoothing and volume normalization to produce directional signals on two buffers. The applied price enum (PRICE_WEIGHTED default=HLCC/4) and volume type (VOLUME_TICK default) feed into the indicator. GetStartBars() from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh determines minimum lookback. Entry is simple (signal on previous bar), but the lookback close-scan loop adds complexity. Position sizing supports 5 margin modes via TradeAlgorithms.mqh which must also be ported.
